record_notes.DCP-LETT-1461F: November 4, 1851 exact ALS. Three complete blocks and sole footnote. Returns signed/witnessed parchment, hopes correctly done. Document identity unknown; editor possible revised will after Annie death is conjecture, not known source subject. Enclosure text and initiating Salt note absent.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-1465F: December 24, 1851 exact ALS. Four blocks and two footnotes. Requests notice to Muckleston executor for repayment after proper interval, earlier if convenient; not current repayment or foreclosure completion. Emma trustees named, Josiah signature appears as distinct P3 concurrence, not Darwin prose. Later 1854 payoff is editorial future. Original December 24 composition and December 25 forwarding described in 1466G differ legitimately.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-1466G: December 26, supplied 1851 ALS. Five blocks and four footnotes. Missing Salt note reports Hanmer notice for next June 25; actual June 1, 1852 payoff only later investment record. Main P2 would conditionally withdraw own Muckleston repayment request because larger capital expected, but reopened P.S. changes mind again and requests notice if Josiah consents. Preserve successive reasoning and last instruction without deleting prior text. Yesterday sent to Josiah establishes December 25 routing for December 24-dated 1465F; neither becomes Salt incoming prompt. Historical burn-note request is quoted content only.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-1499F: January 31, supplied 1853 corroborated by endorsement. Five blocks and three footnotes. Missing Salt note received yesterday gives January 30. Requests sale of both Shrewsbury securities together, not either separately; sale and transfer only future. March transaction and March 28 capital payoff are later. Curacy/house reference unidentified; no fabricated subject detail.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-1506F: March 15, supplied 1853 from wrapper March 28 label. Four blocks and four footnotes. Purchaser now reported found in missing Salt note; transfers enclosed, interest due March 28 only presumed forthcoming. Later interest record does not prove March 15 receipt or transfer fee paid. Wrapper date is not composition date. Charles Wigley informed about bankers indirectly, no preserved incoming here.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-1577F: July 12, supplied 1854 confirmed by endorsement. Four blocks and two footnotes. Salt note explicitly received this morning says 1018 pounds will be paid to London account this day; Darwin current notification is not confirmed bank credit. Gold payment to Salt already reported, distinct from bank arrival. Powis principal provisionally receipted and bond sent about month ago, but interest still not received. Later account records of July 1 principal and interest do not rewrite Darwin present absence claim. Worker paid-into-account summary overstates body future tense.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-1213: After July 12, 1851, XML July 13–31 bound; incomplete ALS starts mid-sentence and has later damaged word. Five surviving blocks, four footnotes and bibliography. Requests capital/income split of 220 pounds already paid; July 12 account entry dates payment evidence, not exact letter. Enclosed Stokes note not surviving. Caroline Swanage note read and appreciated; deleted personal paragraph still Darwin authorial prose, probable Josiah deletion later, not licensed omission or exact deletion date. Both postscripts retained, no missing beginning reconstructed.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-1488: October 21, supplied 1852 ALS. Four blocks and three footnotes. Langton warning motivates intended North Western sale, with Emma assets and Darwin own assets not merged. Prior broker letter written but sale authorization to Josiah conditional; alternate broker would cost double commission. Actual October 22 own and October 25 trust sales/losses are later ledger information. Expressed fears and preferences historical, not investment advice or completed transaction.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-1490: November 20, 1852 authorial financial statement ADS, recipient Josiah inferred by Erasmus mention. Seven retained blocks plus raw separator paragraphs, three footnotes and bibliography inspected. Raw HTML already contains diag/ramme broken layout, no actual account table or image. Retain pounds/shillings/pence columns and repeated subtotal sequence: trustees 6471 pounds 18s 6d, Darwin 7130, difference 658 pounds 1s 6d. 87 shares at 24 pounds 10s versus stated 2130 presents arithmetic tension; do not silently recalculate or repair account. Entries dated 1851/1852 are retrospective evidence as of statement, not a newly composed letter on every transaction date. Grounding requires faithful account rendering, not synthetic dialogue.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-1503: February 18, 1853 exact ALS. Eight blocks, five footnotes, bibliography and raw account markup. Prior oral consent to deed custody confirmed in writing; speaker presumed Josiah, not certain. Salt note returned but absent. Body thanks for 84 pounds, apparatus record says 86: retain source discrepancy. P7 cites missing Josiah letter total 180 versus Darwin entries 62+48+60=170, P8 expects silence to confirm; no actual confirmation inferred from absence. Ill William future Monday return, not completed travel. Broken flat account lines preserved and formatting required.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-1379: 25, supplied April 1853 ALS. Seven blocks, three footnotes and bibliography. Conclusive Josiah document received this morning; long letter drafted yesterday made superfluous, not necessarily sent. Intended railway transfer and signed-certificate custody future. P5 presumes declaration applies Owen not Powis; this is corrected in next-day 1380 P4, so retain current mistake and later correction separately. Erasmus legal view reported, Darwin explicitly does not understand trust advantage. Missing original Josiah statements/document cannot be reconstructed from account summaries.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-1568: May 1, supplied 1854 ALS. Three blocks, two footnotes and bibliography. Requests Josiah signature to complete share transfer; promised Muckleston payoff end of month is not realized May receipt, actual July 11 later. Distinguishes ordinary Emma inheritance trust from marriage trust, not own personal money. Brodie interview news welcomed; editor possible mental-health purpose conjectural. Brodie book later July 3 reading not current May knowledge. Footnote from Erasmus April 26, 1853 points to separately read 1516, whose unreceived last two holdings remain explicit.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-1530: September 6, supplied 1853 ALS. Both blocks and sole footnote. New school information acknowledged after long silence; supports proposed memorial and plans vestry attendance, not school opening. Interest of deceased second baronet heard from others, recipient is third baronet, later John scientist is separate person. No full incoming notice survives.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-1536: October 11, supplied 1853 ALS. Five blocks and five full footnotes. Missing Lubbock note received this morning; Darwin infers agreement from oral remarks but sees risk project fails if deed altered. Innes reported position, Poor Law Commissioners letter tenor, National Society requirements and possible funding are described through Darwin understanding, not reproduced complete legal documents or modern law. Willingness to admit dissenters without objectionable doctrine reported as Innes promise, not proven policy implemented. Appeal and withheld donations proposed safeguards, not completed actions.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-1563: March 28, supplied 1854 ALS. Five blocks, six footnotes and bibliography. Regrets unexpected opposition in Guardian appointment learned Saturday night, preserves account of previous nomination and withdrawal after Fox misunderstanding. Innes nomination not school trusteeship; Darwin own declined candidacy separate. Vestry attendance tomorrow prospective, no election outcome. Fox, Smith and Ainslie identities are editorial probable/either/possible, not certain named entities. No incoming Lubbock objection text preserved.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-1628: January 10, supplied 1855 ALS. Three blocks, two footnotes and bibliography. January 9 long oral interview with Baugh reported; Darwin fears little success. Commissioners application threatened unless compromise, Court of Equity threat doubted. Workmen stopped by Lubbock report; conversion to cottages and reinvestment conditional future, not actual conversion. Baugh complaint of prior ignorance until September is his claim. Footnote schools funding reconstruction explicitly likely because early records absent, not verified institutional record.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-1631: Monday 15, supplied January 1855 ALS. Four blocks and two footnotes. Lubbock note received January 14; Darwin visited Baugh after breakfast January 15. Baugh now says case already laid before Commissioners, contrary to earlier threatened stage. Further Court of Equity and local law-cost subscription conditional; lawyer opinion reported through Baugh, not court judgment. Archbishop not discussed explicitly. London house taken, Thursday move and scientific meetings future, later itinerary not proof current attendance.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-1042: Explicit accepted primary full-source reading reused after matching note, ledger and source hashes. Friday, conjectured August 20, 1847. Two messages thanked, missing enclosed letter says fifty-one pounds settles railway calls, payment now requested. Fifteen-pound repayment and forty-pound source uncertain. P3-7 broken account layout has no substantive HTML table/image. About four hundred available, two shares proposed, remembered prices uncertain: preserve apparent count/arithmetic inconsistency rather than substituting later four-share purchase from apparatus. Raw MathML in P10 is three and a half percent, flattened as 312. Monmouth debenture withdrawal desired but term unknown; later five-percent seven-year lock is future editorial context.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-1111F: Explicit accepted primary full-source reading reused after matching note, ledger and source hashes. Sunday, conjectured August 22, 1847 from preceding trade, not independently exact. Missing Stokes enclosure received and acknowledged; two-hundred-pound advance calls requested unless Josiah objects. Actual HTML table preserves separate pound and trailing shilling columns: Paid 3742 / 10, Call 200 / blank, Total 3942 / 10. Do not turn these into decimal currency or include footnote marker four in amount. Stokes payment requested, not demonstrated settled. Erasmus to inquire about calls; later additional shares prospective. Leith Hill Place purchase congratulated, fixed for life is contemporary expectation.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-1142: Explicit accepted primary full-source reading reused after matching note, ledger and source hashes. Sunday, July 1848 inferred from calls and account book. Forty-five pounds due plus anticipated one hundred sixty-two, unable to advance two hundred seven. Earlier fully-paid assumption contradicted and company overcharge reported acknowledged, actual company reply missing. Nine twenty-five-pound shares and capital/interest allocation queried, trustees asked for records. Two-page enclosure mentioned in XML and aggregate figures in footnote, but full enclosure absent from body and scholarly sections. Do not manufacture it from editorial totals. Later August 1 entry on July payment does not resolve exact Sunday or receipt.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-1103F: Explicit accepted primary full-source reading reused after matching note, ledger and source hashes. July 27, 1849 from endorsement. Brother documents received yesterday and returned to Salt; July 26 only under assigned letter date. Estate subject is editorial may, not proven identity; documents not transcribed. Returning enclosure not source-complete response to its content.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-1269F: Explicit accepted primary full-source reading reused after matching note, ledger and source hashes. November 12, supplied 1849. Brother reports future Powis mortgage payoff by next Lady Day, possibly sooner, plus promised ten-thousand-pound cash. Requests new twenty-to-thirty-thousand-pound security and states security preference, no realized repayment or reinvestment. Half existing twenty thousand described as Emma trust, half own, a contemporary attribution. Later account entries and absent ten-thousand-pound receipt record remain separate. Footnote calls Lady Day March 24, conflicting with external calendar convention; preserve literal Lady Day and hold any normalized event date. No forecast becomes actual receipt.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-1271F: Explicit accepted primary full-source reading reused after matching note, ledger and source hashes. November 19, 1849 endorsed. Explicitly answers missing Salt note of November 13, agrees to leave February for investment search and hopes success. No preserved incoming query or completed transaction.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-1319F: Explicit accepted primary full-source reading reused after matching note, ledger and source hashes. April 7, 1850 endorsed. Missing Salt sympathy/assistance and offer of safe three-to-three-and-a-half-thousand-pound investment accepted on trust without party names. Will write today to Robarts for six-thousand-five-hundred-pound Exchequer Bills; intention not proven purchase. Later April 17 Corbett investment is a distinct editorial event. Possible relation to brother cash only conjectural, no incoming bank instruction recovered.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-1373: Explicit accepted primary full-source reading reused after matching note, ledger and source hashes. December 1, supplied 1850. Thanks for money sent to Robarts. Two Salt letters No I and No II read/forwarded but absent; No I answers own earlier financial letter, No II warns of possible forced sale. Willingness to transfer five-thousand-pound shares depends on costs and advantages. Legal uncertainty and hope lawyer mistaken are attributed beliefs, not completed forced sale or transfer. Request to leave shares with co-trustee Erasmus while Josiah away is conditional administration. Fresh 1372 is own prior outgoing letter, not one of the missing Salt prompts.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-942: Explicit accepted primary full-source reading reused after matching note, ledger and source hashes. Prior full primary reading reused with matched hashes. Friday January16[1846] thanks Lubbock for land consent; sheltered walk gardening future. January12 agreement is21year lease of1.5acres at£1/12annually, not12acres from flattened fraction. Agreement not surviving letter prompt or proof planting completed.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-1210: Explicit accepted primary full-source reading reused after matching note, ledger and source hashes. December 1848–1849 mourning-stationery range, not necessarily two discrete Decembers. Thanks for drawings and coins; cannot identify English stone, only compares its appearance with shell-rich tropical island/coral-reef material. Do not supply a firm geological identification or exact receipt day. No surviving Lubbock prompt.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-1212: Explicit accepted primary full-source reading reused after matching note, ledger and source hashes. Wednesday within December 1848–1849 range. Schoolroom permission note known, Nash appointment prospective. Drawing reportedly sent but explicitly not received. Son had called twice unsuccessfully; microscope discussion Thursday or Friday depends on health. Missed Adams invitation, meteor paper thanked without explicit complete reading. Do not sequence this letter before 1210 solely from drawing absence versus drawings receipt; identity of the objects is unproved. Nash and Adams identifications in apparatus remain tentative.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-1380: Explicit accepted primary full-source reading reused after matching note, ledger and source hashes. April 26, 1853 supplied month/year; Darwin day 26 is original. Reports Jos second letter and intended transfer to restore Emma trust holdings, while professing uncertainty. Sends trust-property list and declaration, asks Erasmus acknowledgement and perhaps return. Requested Newcastle/Carlisle transfer and future certificate are not completion or receipt. Tank/siphon planning is a separate subject ending in a marked missing section. Prior Erasmus tank calculations are missing; old 727 concerns geological elevations, not this hydraulic design. Earl Powis, Major Owen and their mortgage declarations remain distinct. Erasmus 1516 is an answer to this request, not its prompt.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-1516: Explicit accepted primary full-source reading reused after matching note, ledger and source hashes. April 26, 1853 incoming acknowledgement specifically answers the trust statement and requested document acknowledgement in 1380. Lists settlements and securities at the bankers, but P9 explicitly says the last two railway holdings are NOT yet received. Preserve that scope across list rows and non-decimal currency. Later May 1 transfer in apparatus is not April 26 possession. Four pages found in the envelope are later notes from 1856, 1871 and 1879, not contemporary enclosures to be merged into this letter. Same-day reply can establish Erasmus access to the statement by April 26; it does not establish Darwin reading the answer then.

reading_method: Root independently read complete surviving new source bodies, metadata constraints, exclusions, footnotes, scholarly sections and bibliography. Actual special markup and figures inspected where present. Reused explicit accepted primary readings only after matching source and accepted evidence hashes. Historical decisions and notes are handwritten; validation packages evidence rather than adjudicating it.
